subject: Request: weighted uptime credit & third-party attribution for 2027-02-21 service slowdown
messages:
From: Samira Patel <ops@helixhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeWorks Support <infra@edgeworks.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partial degradation during maintenance window (2027-02-21) — request for credit

Hi Tessa,

We saw a spike in p95/p99 latency for our /v1/generate endpoint between 2027-02-21T22:41:00Z and 2027-02-21T23:18:00Z (UTC). It manifested as sustained ~600–900ms p95 vs our baseline ~120ms. Error rates did not increase materially, but a number of user requests timed out at the client layer.

Per our SLA we opened a ticket and EdgeWorks support confirmed there was a CDN edge routing flapping event that coincided with the window. They suggested some traffic fell back to a ‘slow path’ which increased egress latencies.

We believe this is not solely a Helix-side impact — it affected requests routed to Redwood via EdgeWorks. We are requesting an uptime credit consistent with partial degradation guidance in the contract and would like Redwood to:

- confirm how the 37-minute window should be counted against uptime (full outage vs weighted partial-degradation),
- share Redwood’s probe and SLO calculation for that interval, and
- confirm whether third-party (EdgeWorks) attribution will affect the final credit.

I’ve attached a CSV of sample client-side latencies and a trace dump (zipped). Requesting a response by EOD 2027-02-23 so we can reconcile internally.

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Sr. SRE — Helix Health
attachments: helix_latency_sample.csv, helix_trace_20270221.zip
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <ops@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation during maintenance window (2027-02-21) — request for credit

Hi Samira — thanks for the data and the heads up. I’ve looped in Ben to coordinate commercial recourse and Marissa from SRE to dig into trace/probe evidence.

Prelim notes:
- We see an increase in latency in our edge telemetry that overlaps the window you provided, but our internal serving logs show that the majority of tokens were still generated successfully (no elevated 5xx). That pattern often aligns with upstream egress variability vs a Redwood runtime fault.
- Our SLA defines \"partial degradation\" as a measurable increase in latency affecting a measurable fraction of requests; credits may be weighted rather than full outage credits. We need to reconcile the fraction of impacted requests and the duration.

Marissa — can you pull the per-route probe samples and the SLO calculation (p95 weighting) for HLX's routes during 2027-02-21T22:30:00Z — 2027-02-21T23:30:00Z and confirm whether the latency signature matches an internal slow path or egress-pressured behavior?

Samira — could you confirm which IP ranges/edge PoPs you observed the routing flaps on? EdgeWorks included a reference id in their alert (EW-1824) which might help cross-referencing.

I’ll propose a temporary cadence: we’ll aim to have a consolidated position and proposed credit calculation by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0112

From: Samira Patel <ops@helixhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeWorks Support <infra@edgeworks.io>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation during maintenance window (2027-02-21) — request for credit

Tessa,

Thanks — follow-ups below:
- EdgeWorks identified PoPs: us-west-2-pop7 and us-west-2-pop9. Their incident EW-1824 notes a BGP flap and transient cache-miss flood that lasted ~28 minutes but the client-observed tail latency persisted for ~37 minutes while traffic rebalanced.
- I’ve attached an anonymized list of impacted request IDs and timestamps (see helix_latency_sample.csv).
- We are proposing a weighted credit: treat the 37-minute window as 28 minutes attributable to EdgeWorks (third party) and a residual 9 minutes as a performance degradation in the request path where Redwood’s routing fallback increased p95 for some fraction of requests.

Helix’s suggested calculation: apply a 60% weight to the residual 9-minute window (creditable duration = 9 * 0.6 = 5.4 minutes) and then run the standard outage-to-credit conversion defined in section 4.2 of our SLA. The rationale is that while the majority was third-party, Redwood’s fallback increased client-side impact.

Let us know whether Redwood will accept a weighted approach (and if so, how Redwood calculates the impacted fraction).

Samira
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <ops@helixhealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partial degradation during maintenance window (2027-02-21) — request for credit

Samira — thanks for the clear proposal and data. I’ll summarize Redwood’s position and next steps so we can converge quickly: 

1) Attribution: our preliminary SRE review (Marissa) shows the dominant signal aligning with EdgeWorks PoP instabilities. Because the initial cause originated upstream, our standard practice is to exclude third-party faults when they meet the documented third-party exclusion criteria.

2) Partial-degradation weighting: that said, we acknowledge a residual client impact during the tail of the window where our routing fallback increased observed p95 for a subset of requests. We are open to a weighted credit approach.

3) Proposed calculation (Redwood): we will take your proposed split (28 minutes EdgeWorks, 9 minutes residual). For the 9-minute residual, Redwood will compute the impacted request fraction using our route-level request histogram. From a preliminary sample, the fraction of requests over the p95 threshold in that 9-minute window is ~45%. Applying that fraction yields creditable minutes = 9 * 0.45 = 4.05 minutes.

4) Credit conversion: we will apply the SLA conversion table to 4.05 minutes and share an itemized credit ledger. We expect that to result in a partial credit worth ~0.018% of monthly recurring fees (subject to exact conversion).

5) Goodwill offer: to move forward quickly and maintain application experience, Redwood will also provide a one-time 2 months of free reserved inference credits (applies to HLX-2025-R3 committed tier) while we finalize the ledger.

Next steps: Marissa will attach the detailed per-route histogram and timestamped probe samples; Connor will produce the formal credit ledger and calculation. We’ll target delivery by EOD Wed 2027-02-24. If that timeline works, we can close once you confirm acceptance of the weighted method.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
